title: Nvidia's Leadership Crisis Pulls Nasdaq Futures Lower
dek: Nasdaq futures are down about 0.8% after reports that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang, cutting short Wednesday's AI rally. Treasuries reopen after Veterans Day with the 10-year near 5%, as traders still expect a December Fed rate hike.
quick: Nvidia fell about 8% after hours and is lower again pre-market after reports that its board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang. As of early Thursday, no decision had been announced.
Nasdaq futures are down about 0.8% and S&P 500 futures about 0.35%. Dow futures are slightly higher.
Bond trading resumes after the holiday: the 10-year yield is about 5.00% and the 2-year about 4.76%. Futures still price a December Fed hike as very likely.
AI cloud stocks are giving back gains: CoreWeave is down about 5% to 6% after jumping nearly 25% Wednesday, and Nebius is lower despite beating revenue forecasts.
Europe's Stoxx 600 is at a record as money moves away from AI stocks. UK GDP grew 0.7% last quarter.
Today: jobless claims at 8:30 a.m. ET, six Fed speakers, a 30-year bond auction, and Cisco and Applied Materials after the close.

blocks.head: Nvidia's board weighs removing Jensen Huang
blocks.what: The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove founder and CEO Jensen Huang. The board met Wednesday evening, and no decision had been announced as of early Thursday. Huang admitted on Sunday to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence has identified as a Chinese asset, and the company hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to investigate. The New York Times then reported a second relationship, with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. Nvidia shares fell more than 8% after hours. They had closed up 2.9% at $173.73 on Wednesday.
blocks.why: Nvidia is one of the largest companies in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, so its drop is the main reason index futures are lower. The selling is spreading to companies tied to Nvidia through supply and financing deals, including CoreWeave, IREN and Coherent. Evercore analysts said Nvidia has no obvious succession plan or clear second-in-command, which adds to the uncertainty.
blocks.watch: Any board statement could come at any time, and Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday, November 17.

blocks.head: Fed hike bets hold as the bond market reopens
blocks.what: Treasuries trade today for the first time since Tuesday's October CPI report: prices rose 0.4% and core prices 0.3%, both above forecasts. The 2-year yield jumped as much as 20 basis points Tuesday, its biggest one-day move since April 2025. Fed Governor Christopher Waller backs a December hike and said a half-point move should be discussed if core inflation ran near 0.3%. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called the data 'borderline disturbing' but did not commit to a December vote.
blocks.why: Higher expected rates weigh most on richly valued growth stocks, gold and crypto, and they support the dollar. CME FedWatch snapshots after the CPI report put the odds of a quarter-point hike at the December 8 to 9 meeting at roughly 85% to 100%. Those snapshots put the odds of a half-point move at about 10% to 15%.
blocks.watch: Six Fed officials speak today. Listen for whether any of them support a half-point hike.

blocks.head: The AI cloud rally reverses one day later
blocks.what: CoreWeave jumped 24.7% Wednesday to $60.77, its biggest gain since mid-2025, after third-quarter revenue rose 168% to $3.66 billion and it raised its 2026 outlook. Pre-market Thursday it is down about 5% to 6%. Nebius reported before the open: revenue of $980.8 million beat forecasts of about $907.5 million, and it posted an adjusted profit of 30 cents a share, while analysts had expected a loss. Its 2026 revenue guidance of $3 billion to $3.4 billion came in slightly below the consensus midpoint, and the shares fell.
blocks.why: These companies rent out Nvidia chips and borrow heavily to do it, so they react strongly to Nvidia news and to interest rates. The swings show how much the Nasdaq still depends on confidence in AI spending.
blocks.watch: Watch whether Wednesday's chip-stock gains hold once trading opens.

blocks.head: Washington pressure on chip exports to China grows
blocks.what: The scandal has revived calls in Congress for tighter limits on advanced AI chip sales to China. CNBC reported that House China committee chairman John Moolenaar wants chip export controls added to the annual defense bill. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked the administration to preserve its records on Nvidia and China, according to the Wall Street Journal. Megaspeed, a Singapore company at the center of a US probe into restricted Nvidia chips reaching China, issued its first public statement Thursday.
blocks.why: Tighter export rules would hurt US chipmakers' China sales. WSJ reported that some Chinese chip stocks drew support on bets that local suppliers could win share from Nvidia.
blocks.watch: President Trump is expected to meet Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18 to 19, according to CNBC and the South China Morning Post.

blocks.head: MSCI will remove Strategy from its indexes
blocks.what: MSCI published the final list from its November index review, and Strategy, the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, is being removed from its indexes after the November 30 close. Japan's Metaplanet is also being removed. The change follows MSCI's new rule that excludes companies whose main business is holding assets. Strategy shares fell pre-market, according to the WSJ.
blocks.why: Funds that track MSCI indexes will no longer need to own Strategy, which could force selling around month-end. The news adds to pressure on Bitcoin, which is already down on Fed-hike bets.

blocks.text: Asia

Most Asian markets fell as the Nvidia news hit chip and AI stocks across the region. Japan's Nikkei fell about 0.7%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng lost about 1.3%, and Shanghai slipped about 0.7%. Taiwan, home to many Nvidia suppliers, had the biggest drop, with the Taiex down 2.6%, according to AP. South Korea's Kospi dipped 0.2%. Foxconn, Nvidia's biggest server assembler, reported continued strong earnings growth on AI hardware demand, but that did not stop the selling across the region.
Europe

Europe is gaining instead. The Stoxx 600 hit another record, up about 0.4%, and Germany's DAX is up about 0.8%. Reuters said Europe has benefited from having few AI stocks, as investors move money out of AI names in the US and Asia. It also cited LSEG data showing European companies on track for about 25% quarterly profit growth, the strongest in four years. Energy companies account for much of that growth. The UK reported third-quarter GDP growth of 0.7%, in line with estimates and its fastest pace in about two and a half years. The FTSE 100 is up about 0.4%.
Currencies

Currency markets are quiet. The dollar index is flat near 102.9, holding its gain from Tuesday's inflation report. The euro is little changed around $1.109. The yen is near 159.7 per dollar. The pound is around $1.327: it stayed below $1.33 even after the strong GDP report. China's yuan is steady near 6.67 per dollar.

Futures show money moving out of tech and into other sectors. Nasdaq futures are down about 0.8% and S&P 500 futures about 0.35%, both pulled lower by Nvidia's weight. Dow futures are up about 0.1%, because the Dow uses share prices rather than company size to weight its members, so Nvidia counts for much less. On Wednesday the S&P 500 rose 1.3% to 7,619, the Nasdaq 1.6% to 25,466 and the Dow 0.5% to 52,486. CoreWeave's results led that rally.

The VIX volatility index rose about 0.8 points to 18.3. The main question for the open is whether the selling stays in AI stocks or spreads to the broader market. Europe's record high and slightly higher Dow futures suggest it is mostly limited to AI stocks for now.

Treasuries are trading again after Wednesday's Veterans Day closure, and yields are slightly higher. The 2-year is about 4.76%, up about 4 basis points. The 10-year is about 5.00%, up about 1 basis point. The 30-year is about 5.35%, little changed. The 2-year is most sensitive to Fed expectations, and it has led the move since the CPI report. The gap between the 2-year and 10-year is now about 24 basis points, and the 30-year is about 35 basis points above the 10-year.

Fed officials have mostly leaned toward raising rates. Waller backs a December hike and is open to a half-point move. Goolsbee described the October inflation numbers as concerning but did not say how he would vote. According to CME FedWatch snapshots after the CPI report, futures price a December quarter-point hike as very likely, roughly 85% to 100% depending on the time of the reading. They also put about a 10% to 15% chance on a half-point move. Friday's producer price report is the next big data test.
The 30-year bond auction at 1 p.m. ET tests demand for long-term debt with yields above 5%. A weak auction could push long-term yields higher.

blocks.text: Wednesday's sectors

Technology led Wednesday with a gain of about 3.1%, as chip stocks recovered on CoreWeave's results and Nvidia's rebound. Energy was second, up about 1.8%, as oil rose after Iran denied it was negotiating with Washington. Industrials gained about 1.3%. The weakest sectors were roughly flat: consumer discretionary slipped about 0.05%, while real estate and health care barely moved. With tech the most exposed to Nvidia, it is the sector most likely to give back gains today.
Pre-market movers

items: Nvidia: down sharply after reports that its board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang. It fell more than 8% after hours, and pre-market declines have ranged from about 5% to 8%.
CoreWeave, IREN and Coherent: lower along with Nvidia. CoreWeave is down about 5% to 6% after Wednesday's 25% jump.
Nebius: lower even though revenue and profit beat forecasts. Its 2026 sales guidance came in slightly below the consensus midpoint. It projected 2027 revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion.
Strategy: lower after MSCI confirmed it will be removed from MSCI indexes after November 30.
Tetra Tech: up about 8% to 10% after quarterly earnings of 49 cents a share on $1.34 billion in revenue beat estimates.
Franco-Nevada: roughly flat after reporting third-quarter earnings of $1.89 a share on revenue of about $549 million.

blocks.text: Oil

Oil is lower. WTI is near $85.80, down about 0.8%, and Brent is near $92.10, down about 0.7%. Brent rose nearly 3% Wednesday after Iran denied it was negotiating with the US, which reversed some of the early-week drop on hopes for a deal. Reports say Brent is down about 21% since the start of November, as markets have bet that diplomacy could ease disruptions to supplies from the Iran conflict. The weekly government oil inventory report comes at noon ET today, a day late because of the holiday. Analysts expect a drop of about 600,000 barrels.
Gold

Gold is down about 1% to around $3,958 an ounce and has fallen below $4,000. With the 10-year yield near 5% and a Fed hike expected, gold faces more competition from bonds that pay interest. Gold was above $4,100 as recently as Monday.
Crypto

Bitcoin is down about 1.7% to around $73,300, and Ether is down about 1.8% to around $2,040. Higher rate expectations after the CPI report have hurt crypto all week. TradingKey reported that US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $1.4 billion in outflows since November 5. MSCI's decision to remove Strategy from its indexes adds more pressure on Bitcoin-related stocks.

Third-quarter earnings of $1.89 a share. Gold royalty stocks are under pressure as gold falls below $4,000.

blocks.text: Friday brings October producer prices at 8:30 a.m. ET. Forecasts call for headline PPI up 0.4% and core up 0.3%, after much bigger gains of 1.3% and 0.7% in September. A hot reading would add to bets on a half-point December hike. Fed officials Collins, Logan, Bowman, Daly and Jefferson also speak Friday. Beyond this week, Nvidia's earnings next Tuesday, November 17, could matter even more than usual depending on the board's decision. President Trump's expected meeting with Xi Jinping at APEC in Shenzhen on November 18 to 19 will show whether chip export rules come up after the scandal. The Fed's next decision is December 9.

bottom_line: The morning is defined by one company: Nvidia's leadership uncertainty is pulling the Nasdaq lower while the Dow and Europe hold up. Treasury yields near 5% and expectations of a Fed hike leave little support for tech if the selling continues.
